summary: @servicetitan/marketing-widgets 1.0.3 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle
details: The package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. `setup.mjs` (itself renamed with obfuscator.io-style identifiers) checks for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads Bun v1.3.13 from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<target>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle featuring a rotated string-array (`WV8StW`) and custom permuted-alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`) — the standard obfuscator.io shape. The filename is a cover story: the file contains no math-related API and is referenced only by the preinstall dropper. The rest of the tarball (`dist/`, `src/`) contains a plausible ServiceTitan React marketing-widgets library, but that legitimate code has no need for a second language runtime or an opaque bundle to be executed before install completes. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a shipped obfuscated payload at install time — separate from the package's advertised purpose — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and executes attacker-controlled code on every installer's machine before any import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
